title: Prolonged pregnancy, membrane sweep and induction
blurb: Support informed decisions about sweeps and induction under NICE NG207, choose the method from the Bishop score, and care for women who decline.
question: Chloe, 41+2 weeks in an uncomplicated first pregnancy, has had a membrane sweep. She does not want her labour induced. How should the midwife respond, and what can be offered from 42 weeks?

teach.body: Formally: NICE NG207 says give women with uncomplicated pregnancies every opportunity to go into spontaneous labour, explain that some risks rise after 41+0 weeks (caesarean birth, neonatal intensive care admission, stillbirth and neonatal death), and discuss induction from 41+0. In plain English: most babies arrive on their own by 42 weeks. From 41 weeks the balance shifts, so the midwife sets out the options honestly and the woman decides.

teach.h: Spontaneous labours started by each gestation
teach.caption: Cumulative proportion of spontaneous labours (NG207 table 1, HES/MSDS 2019–20).
Check there is no low-lying placenta on previous scans before a sweep or induction (NG207 1.7.6).

teach.body: Explain that induction is a medical intervention: vaginal examinations, a narrower choice of birth place and possibly no birthing pool, possible assisted birth with a higher risk of anal sphincter injury, risk of hyperstimulation, often more pain and a longer stay. Give time to think and talk with others. She can proceed, delay, decline or stop, and her decision is respected and recorded even if professionals disagree.

head: Component
What is assessed
rows: Head level relative to ischial spines
teach.caption: A score of 8 or more generally means the cervix is ready to dilate; NG207 uses 6 or less versus more than 6 to choose the method.

children.label: Dinoprostone or low-dose oral misoprostol
children.sub: or mechanical (balloon) if drugs unsuitable or she prefers

children.label: Amniotomy + IV oxytocin
children.sub: she can choose to delay or decline oxytocin

teach.caption: Previous caesarean: dinoprostone and misoprostol are contraindicated by their licences (uterine rupture); a mechanical method may be considered (NG207 1.2.17, 1.3.8).

steps.label: Too many or too long contractions

teach.caption: Mechanical methods cause hyperstimulation less often; misoprostol hyperstimulation may be harder to reverse (NG207 1.3.5, 1.7.1).

teach.body: The midwife respects Chloe's decision, discusses her options from now (expectant management or caesarean birth) and records her choice. She offers additional monitoring from 42 weeks, such as twice-weekly CTG and ultrasound of the deepest amniotic pool, explaining that monitoring is a snapshot and cannot reliably predict or prevent stillbirth. Chloe can revisit her decision at every review and should call at once if her baby's movements change.

teach.text: Castor oil, hot baths, sex, herbal supplements, acupuncture, homeopathy and enemas are NOT supported for inducing labour (NG207 1.4.2). And a membrane sweep is offered after 39+0, while induction is discussed from 41+0: do not swap them.

items: Every opportunity for spontaneous labour; most start before 42+0.
Risks rise after 41+0: caesarean, NICU admission, stillbirth and neonatal death.
Sweep at visits after 39+0 with verbal consent; discuss induction from 41+0.
Bishop 6 or less: prostaglandin, or mechanical if drugs unsuitable; over 6: amniotomy + oxytocin.
Hyperstimulation: assess baby, stop doses, remove pessary, consider tocolysis.
Declined induction: respect, record, offer monitoring from 42 weeks.

summary: You can now explain the timing of sweeps and induction discussions, describe what induction involves, and choose a method from the Bishop score. You can also manage hyperstimulation and support a woman who declines induction with additional monitoring from 42 weeks.

A.q: According to NICE NG207, when should a midwife offer a membrane sweep to a woman with an uncomplicated pregnancy?
options: At the 36-week appointment for all women
At any antenatal visit from 37+0 weeks
At the 38-week appointment if she wishes
A.why: NG207 1.3.2: at antenatal visits after 39+0 weeks, discuss membrane sweeping and obtain verbal consent before doing it.

whyNot.0: 36 weeks is too early for a sweep under NG207.
whyNot.1: NG207 sets the point as after 39+0, not 37+0.
whyNot.2: 38 weeks is before the NG207 threshold of 39+0.

A.q: From what gestation should induction of labour be discussed with a woman whose pregnancy is uncomplicated?
A.why: NG207 1.2.4: discuss that induction from 41+0 weeks may reduce the risks of continuing pregnancy, alongside its impact on her birth experience.

whyNot.0: 40+0 is the due date, not the NG207 point for discussing induction.
whyNot.2: 42+0 is when additional monitoring is offered to women who decline.
whyNot.3: 39+0 is when membrane sweeps are offered.

A.q: Abi, 41+3 weeks, has a Bishop score of 8. Which method of induction should be offered?
A.why: NG207 1.3.9: for a Bishop score of more than 6, offer amniotomy and an intravenous oxytocin infusion.

whyNot.1: Dinoprostone is offered when the Bishop score is 6 or less.
whyNot.2: Misoprostol is offered when the Bishop score is 6 or less.
whyNot.3: Mechanical methods are considered with a Bishop score of 6 or less.

B.q: Dana, 41+3 weeks, has decided not to have her labour induced. What should the midwife offer?
options: Daily CTG at home from 41+3 weeks
Admission to hospital until labour starts
A growth scan before she goes home
B.why: NG207 1.2.7: discuss additional fetal monitoring from 42 weeks, such as twice-weekly CTG and ultrasound of maximum amniotic pool depth, for women who choose not to be induced.

whyNot.0: Daily home CTG is not the NG207 monitoring schedule.
whyNot.1: Admission until labour is not recommended for a woman declining induction.
whyNot.3: A growth scan is not the monitoring NG207 describes.

B.q: During induction with a dinoprostone vaginal delivery system, Mel has 6 contractions in 10 minutes and the fetal heart rate is decelerating. What should the midwife do?
options: Remove the system, assess the baby, consider tocolysis
Start an oxytocin infusion to regulate the contractions
Continue CTG and give the next prostaglandin dose on time
Perform an amniotomy and wait for progress
B.why: NG207 1.5.3 and 1.7.1: with hyperstimulation, assess the baby with continuous CTG, give no more doses, remove any vaginal pessary or delivery system and consider tocolysis.

whyNot.2: Further doses are withheld when there is hyperstimulation.
whyNot.3: Amniotomy does not reduce contraction frequency and delays treatment.

B.q: Sophie had a caesarean birth 3 years ago and now chooses induction at 41+2 weeks. Her Bishop score is 4. Which method may be considered?
B.why: NG207 1.3.8 and 1.2.17: consider a mechanical method when pharmacological methods are unsuitable, such as after a previous caesarean; dinoprostone and misoprostol licences contraindicate their use with a uterine scar.

whyNot.0: Dinoprostone is contraindicated by its licence in women with a uterine scar.
whyNot.2: Misoprostol is contraindicated by its licence in women with a uterine scar.
whyNot.3: Intravenous oxytocin alone is not supported as an induction method (NG207 1.4.1).

C.q: Before offering Grace a membrane sweep at 40+1 weeks, what must the midwife check in her records?
options: A normal glucose tolerance test result
A negative group B streptococcus swab
A full blood count from the last 2 weeks
No low-lying placenta on previous scans
C.why: NG207 1.7.6: check there is no evidence of a low-lying placenta on previous scans before membrane sweeping and before induction.

whyNot.0: A glucose test result does not affect whether a sweep is safe.
whyNot.1: GBS status does not need to be confirmed before a sweep.
whyNot.2: A recent FBC is not a prerequisite for a sweep.

C.q: Kirsty, 40+5 weeks, asks what might help her labour to start. Which option is supported by NICE NG207?
C.why: NG207 1.3.1–1.3.2: a membrane sweep after 39+0 weeks may make it more likely that labour starts without other methods.

whyNot.0: NG207 1.4.2: evidence does not support castor oil.
whyNot.1: NG207 1.4.2: evidence does not support hot baths.
whyNot.3: NG207 1.4.2: evidence does not support sexual intercourse for induction.

C.q: After vaginal dinoprostone, Lily's contractions begin. A CTG is normal and she is assessed as low risk. What fetal monitoring should follow?
options: Intermittent auscultation unless CTG is indicated
Continuous CTG from now until the baby is born
No fetal monitoring until labour is established
C.why: NG207 1.5.3: if the CTG is confirmed normal and she is considered low risk, use intermittent auscultation unless there are clear indications for CTG.

whyNot.1: Continuous CTG is not needed if the trace is normal and she is low risk.
whyNot.2: This is not an NG207 monitoring schedule.
whyNot.3: The baby's wellbeing is still assessed once contractions begin.

reteach.title: Three gates: 39, 41 and 42
reteach.question: Picture three gates in late pregnancy. What happens at each one, and who decides whether to go through?

blocks.body: At 39+0 the midwife offers a sweep at each visit, with verbal consent. At 41+0 she discusses induction: risks of waiting, what induction involves and the alternatives. At 42+0, if the woman has declined induction, she offers extra monitoring. At every gate the woman decides, and her decision is respected and recorded.

blocks.text: Induction method follows the Bishop score: 6 or less ripens the cervix first; more than 6 goes straight to amniotomy and oxytocin.

explain.body: Labour usually starts before 42+0. Beyond 41+0 the chance of caesarean birth, neonatal intensive care admission, and stillbirth or neonatal death increases, which is why induction is discussed from 41+0.

test.q: Which outcome does NICE NG207 list as becoming more likely as pregnancy continues beyond 41+0 weeks?
test.why: NG207 1.2.3: risks after 41+0 include caesarean birth, neonatal intensive care admission, and stillbirth and neonatal death.

whyNot.0: Corticosteroids are for preterm birth, not prolonged pregnancy.
whyNot.2: Rhesus sensitisation is not linked to gestation beyond 41 weeks.
whyNot.3: Placenta praevia is diagnosed on scan and is not caused by prolonged pregnancy.

explain.body: A vaginal examination in which the midwife sweeps a finger around the cervix to separate the membranes. It may make labour more likely to start. Explain possible pain, discomfort and bleeding, and obtain verbal consent; more sweeps can be discussed.

items: Explain benefits and possible discomfort or bleeding

test.q: What type of consent does NICE NG207 say should be obtained before a membrane sweep?
options: Implied consent by attending the visit
test.why: NG207 1.3.2: if she would like a sweep, obtain verbal consent before carrying it out.

whyNot.0: Written consent is not required by NG207 for a sweep.
whyNot.1: A midwife can obtain consent and perform the sweep.
whyNot.2: Attending an appointment is not consent to an examination.

explain.body: A vaginal examination score of cervical dilatation, effacement (or length), position and consistency, and the station of the head relative to the ischial spines. It guides the first method offered.

test.q: Which finding forms part of the Bishop score?
test.why: The Bishop score includes the station of the head in relation to the ischial spines, with dilatation, effacement, position and consistency (NG207 terms).

whyNot.0: The fetal heart rate is assessed by CTG, not the Bishop score.
whyNot.1: Fundal height is an antenatal growth measure.
whyNot.3: Liquor volume is an ultrasound finding, not part of the score.

explain.body: Respect and record the decision, discuss options (expectant management or caesarean birth), offer additional monitoring from 42 weeks, explain its limits, and revisit the decision at each review if she wishes.

test.q: Which monitoring does NICE NG207 describe for women who decline induction from 42 weeks?
options: Twice-weekly CTG and deepest pool depth
Daily kick charts and weekly fundal height
Weekly growth scans and Doppler studies
Twice-daily checks with a home Doppler
test.why: NG207 1.2.7: monitoring might consist of twice-weekly CTG and ultrasound estimation of maximum amniotic pool depth.

whyNot.1: Kick charts and SFH are not the NG207 monitoring schedule.
whyNot.2: Weekly growth scans are not what NG207 describes for this situation.
whyNot.3: Home Dopplers are unreliable and not recommended.
